item.title: Animation Plugins
item.description: The contract An animation driver controls how the preview pane’s title/content reveal, and how an optional header placeholder rotates: interface HawkAnimationDriver { typeTitle(el, text, options?: { isAnchor?: boolean }): unknown; typeContent(el, html, options?): unknown; rotatePlaceholder(el, strings, options?): unknown; stop(controller): void; } typeTitle/typeContent/rotatePlaceholder may return a controller (anything with whatever shape the driver itself understands) or null. Hawk never inspects it — it only ever passes it back into stop(), which runs before every preview re-render and on destroy().

item.title: API reference
item.description: new HawkSearch(config) Option Type Default Description index string — Base path to a Pagefind bundle. Required unless pagefind is given. pagefind object — A pre-loaded Pagefind module, instead of dynamically importing one from index. id string hawk-search-N DOM id for the modal root. triggerSelector string '[data-search-trigger]' Elements that open the modal on click. trigger object — Renders hawk’s own trigger button instead of requiring hand-built markup. See Built-in trigger. container HTMLElement document.

item.title: Changelog
item.description: Changelog Full release history: CHANGELOG.md in the repository, following Keep a Changelog. Hawk is pre-1.0 and hasn’t cut a tagged release yet — the versions there track package.json’s history, not published tags. 0.5.2 — fixed a real, confirmed reflected-XSS vulnerability (the typed search query reached innerHTML unescaped via strings.noResults). 0.5.1 — a real search-results race condition (#searchGeneration), a modal-chrome vertical-squish bug at narrow widths, a table/long-word overflow past the docs site’s TOC, a header overflow at phone widths, and homepage hero/feature-grid alignment and parity polish.

item.title: Density and keyboard navigation
item.description: Density modes params.density picks between three sizing presets: new HawkSearch({ index: '/pagefind/', params: { density: 'fit' }, // 'fit' | 'medium' (default) | 'compact' }); medium — the default sizing (unchanged from before density existed): a fixed-size dialog, 2 columns. fit — a near-viewport dialog (96vw / 92vh), for a dedicated “search page” feel. compact — a smaller dialog, forced to a single column with the preview pane hidden by default — see Reaching the preview pane in compact layouts.

item.title: Downloads
item.description: Choose a release This page lists versions with a published GitLab Release. Choose unminified development assets or minified production assets for each release. Source archives remain separate from generated bundles. Asset provenance. Every download uses a public GitLab release endpoint. The source link beside each asset opens the tagged repository tree used for that release. Release metadata is not available in this preview build. Visit the GitLab releases page for downloads.

item.title: Getting started
item.description: Install npm install @staticcanvas/hawk npm install --save-dev pagefind pagefind is a real dependency — hawk has nothing to search without an index, so it’s installed automatically. @staticcanvas/typeflow is an optional peer dependency, only needed if you use the typeflow theme/animation driver instead of the built-in unstyled/instant ones. Build an index Mark your page’s main content region with data-pagefind-body, and mark chrome you don’t want indexed (nav, header, footer) with data-pagefind-ignore — see Pagefind setup for why this matters.

item.title: Pagefind Setup
item.description: Scope the index before you run it Pagefind indexes whatever it finds in <body> by default. Without scoping, every result gets polluted with your repeated nav/header/footer text, and broad queries surface pages that only matched on chrome, not content. This one step is the difference between a good and a bad hawk setup: <body> <header data-pagefind-ignore>...</header> <main data-pagefind-body> <!-- your actual page content --> </main> <footer data-pagefind-ignore>...</footer> </body> Once at least one element on the site carries data-pagefind-body, Pagefind switches to “ignore everything outside marked regions” mode automatically.

item.title: Pins, the built-in trigger, and attribution
item.description: Pins A pin toggle renders on every result row by default (enablePins: true) — clicking it doesn’t navigate or trigger onSelect, just pins the result: new HawkSearch({ index: '/pagefind/', enablePins: true, // default pinStorageKey: 'hawk:pins', maxPins: 20, }); Pins persist to localStorage as {url, title, isAnchor}[]. The moment at least one exists, a synthetic “Pinned” tab is prepended to the tab list — selecting it lists pins directly with no Pagefind call (they already carry their own title/url), and clears any typed query, since it isn’t a search scope.

item.title: Theming
item.description: The contract A theme is two things: a CSS file that defines --hawk-* custom properties scoped under [data-hawk-theme="<name>"], and a small plugin object: { name: 'my-theme', apply(rootEl) { rootEl.dataset.hawkTheme = 'my-theme'; }, } apply() runs once when HawkSearch mounts. It doesn’t inject the stylesheet — loading the CSS is the consumer’s job, via a <link> tag or import '@staticcanvas/hawk/theme-typeflow/css'. Token list hawk.css (structural, ships with core) reads every color through a --hawk-* custom property with a neutral fallback, so hawk renders — unstyled but usable — with zero theme loaded.
